theorem_authority: Compiled Lean declarations and their transitive axiom reports; Python and prose cannot promote claims
orientation: Delta = frozen population safety cost minus candidate population safety cost; positive means candidate has lower cost

supplied_specification.normalization: One terminal newline added; otherwise unchanged

formal_evidence.dependency_declarations: Each inventory theorem records local_direct_dependencies extracted from compiled type and proof expressions; these are not a full external dependency graph
formal_evidence.semantic_parity: Human-reviewed statement-to-declaration mapping plus fail-closed snapshot/type/hash binding; not an automated proof that arbitrary English is equivalent to Lean

claims.title: Finite multiclass cost-benefit identity
claims.statement: For every finite stratum and outcome type, every normalized nonnegative stratum mass and conditional label law, and every candidate with bounded stratum-dependent costs, the frozen expected cost minus that candidate's expected cost equals the declared mass-weighted linear benefit.
assumptions: Finite S and Y
q_s >= 0 and sum_s q_s = 1
eta_s,y >= 0 and sum_y eta_s,y = 1
All policy costs in [0,1]
Known costs and stratum masses are mathematical inputs, not empirically certified availability
claims.scope: The identity is pointwise for each candidate; candidate type J can be arbitrary. It specializes to finite K>=3 and finite p. It is not a concentration theorem or an estimate from observed batches.

claims.title: Uniform identification criterion
claims.statement: Corrected target: for fixed finite real operators A and G on the full product simplex, uniform identification over every feasible observable fiber is equivalent to ker([B;A]) being contained in ker(G), and to the corresponding row-space inclusion. At one realized fiber use span(F-F) instead.
assumptions: Simplex affine rows B included
Fixed mass-weighted contrast operator G
Uniform over all feasible right-hand sides for the uniform statement
Nonempty realized fiber for a fiber-specific statement
claims.scope: Exact ranks on rational examples are discovery only; boundary fibers need not have affine hull ker([B;A]).
dependencies: Product-simplex relative-interior argument or realized minimal-face proof

claims.title: Minimal admissible supplement
claims.statement: The unrestricted rank increment is not generally the minimum for an independently specified primitive-moment dictionary. The initial three-class dictionary requires two class probabilities although the unrestricted rank increment is one. A replacement theorem must separate the unrestricted benchmark from the admissible dictionary problem.
assumptions: Additional rows independent modulo the existing observable-plus-simplex row space
Admissible dictionary fixed independently of the unknown benefit
No silent target-benefit or answer-encoding oracle
Exact population moments distinguished from finite labeled observations
claims.scope: The unspecified restricted-class equality is withdrawn. A finite exact catalog search does not prove a general minimality theorem or scientific availability.

claims.title: Realized-fiber scalar sign frontier
claims.statement: For one fixed candidate, a nonempty ambiguity fiber and a strictly positive benefit infimum certify lower candidate cost throughout that fiber; a strictly negative supremum certifies lower frozen cost. Otherwise the mathematical guard abstains. Empty fibers yield protocol failure. A concrete three-class fiber has the exact attainable interval [1/5,3/5] and is not point identified.
assumptions: T1 finite normalized bounded-cost model
True conditional label law belongs to the declared fiber for a deployment interpretation
Strict endpoint inequalities; ties do not certify a strict action
Scientific availability of structural moments is separate
claims.scope: Noncomputable mathematical guard; fixed candidate versus frozen only. Restriction index R can be arbitrary for these soundness results; the finite program is a specialization. No general LP implementation equivalence, global multiadapter choice, finite-sample inference, or general extremum-attainment theorem is claimed.

claims.title: Label-free impossibility
claims.statement: The implication from a surviving observable-null contrast direction to opposite strict decisions is false. The checked three-class witness has nonzero null variation but all benefits lie in [1/5,3/5]. A replacement lower bound must assume feasible strict sign crossing and specify forced commitment, power, or abstention loss.
assumptions: Replacement target needs two feasible worlds with identical permitted observables and incompatible strict decisions
Observation model must exclude target-label/risk or answer-equivalent oracles
A 1/2 wrong-decision statement cannot apply unchanged to free abstention
claims.scope: Concrete refutation of the original implication; no corrected general probabilistic, total-variation, or minimax lower bound has been formalized.
dependencies: ThreeClass exact model and feasible worlds

claims.title: Passive delayed-label complexity
claims.statement: Unproved target: matching passive upper and lower label bounds for a precisely declared strict-commitment task under delayed feedback, with safety and useful-commitment guarantees and separate arrival/request/reveal costs.
assumptions: Passive labeled strata iid from q
Explicit margin-separated target family
Non-abstaining success or power condition
Declared delay and stopping model
Range, variance, candidate count, confidence, and contrast geometry tracked
claims.scope: No estimator, confidence region, rate theorem, or statistical simulation has been implemented in this initial track.

claims.title: Adaptive delayed-label complexity
claims.statement: Unproved target: predictable active label acquisition with valid inference and an achievable matching information lower bound for the shared categorical-label experiment, charging requested and returned labels separately from unlabeled waiting.
assumptions: Queries use only prelabel permitted information and returned history
Noninformative delays or a valid censoring model
Appropriate propensity/positivity or conditional-stratum estimator assumptions
Sequential validity at the declared stopping rule
Nontrivial commitment task
claims.scope: No adaptive estimator, confidence sequence, allocation optimality, or matching lower bound is claimed.

claims.title: Strict active-over-passive separation
claims.statement: Unproved target: a strict active label advantage under the same normalized cost family and commitment criterion. Exact asymmetric rare-stratum worlds with benefits +3/512 and -3/512 have been checked; proposed complexity orders are only discovery conjectures.
assumptions: Rare mass rho>0
The same population margin convention for both procedures
Fixed outcome-independent cost construction
No claim of waiting-time savings from label-count savings
Power requirement and delay/concurrency contract fixed
claims.scope: Exact finite worlds are not a passive/active rate proof or simulation. Fixed positive margin cannot be held while rho tends to zero in this bounded rare-only family.

claims.title: Multi-adapter safe controller
claims.statement: Unproved target: simultaneous false-strict-commit control for frozen-versus-candidate and required candidate-versus-candidate comparisons under adaptive delayed labeling, with explicit ties and a nontrivial selection/commitment criterion.
assumptions: All comparisons required by the selected multiadapter decision rule
Valid simultaneous or sequential coverage
Declared multiplicity correction
Predictable query and delay model
No pairwise certificate promoted to global best-candidate selection
claims.scope: The oracle checks separate fixed-candidate bounds only. T4's noncomputable guard does not implement T9, multiplicity, adaptive inference, or a deployment controller.
